national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT). Primary portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); customs administration is integrated under the Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales (AEAT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a resident Spanish SL: (1) incorporate by public deed before a Spanish notary with a minimum capital of EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid; (2) obtain a provisional NIF through Form 036 processed electronically by the notary or the company with AEAT; (3) register the company in the Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry) within two months; (4) file the definitive censal declaration (Form 036/037) within one month of incorporation to obtain the definitive NIF (letter B for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), enroll in the IAE economic activity census under the applicable heading for toy/plush manufacturing, and register for VAT at the start of activity; (5) obtain an electronic certificate (certificado digital) for SEDE access and OSS portals. For a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment making taxable supplies in Spain: apply to AEAT for a non-resident NIF (letter N or W) and, when required under Article 45 LGT, appoint a tax representative before issuing invoices or commencing taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box pass-through election exists for an SL. Applicable statutory options and regimes: (i) reduced 15% corporate income tax rate for newly created entities in the first two tax periods with a positive tax base under Article 29.1 LIS, excluding income not derived from economic activities; (ii) tax consolidation election for qualifying groups with at least 75% ownership (Articles 58-70 LIS); (iii) ETVE holding-company regime for qualifying foreign securities investments (Articles 107-109 LIS); (iv) tax-neutral merger/demerger election (Articles 76-88 LIS); (v) ATAD hybrid-mismatch adjustment rules under Article 15 septies LIS are mandatory and not elective; (vi) the export VAT zero-rating is a statutory exemption that requires no election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by Ley 37/1992 (LIVA) and RD 1624/1992 (RIVA), aligned with EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for established Spanish taxable persons: the SL must register and file VAT from its first taxable supply. For non-established EU suppliers, intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C cross-border digital services trigger Spanish registration only when the annual Union-wide threshold of EUR 10,000 is exceeded; below that threshold home-country VAT applies. Non-EU non-established suppliers must register in Spain without any threshold before making a taxable supply. Import VAT is payable at customs on all importations regardless of value.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain uses obligation-based structured digital invoicing rather than full invoice pre-clearance. The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) mandates real-time electronic filing of VAT ledger data only for taxpayers with annual turnover above EUR 6,000,000, VAT groups, or REDEME opt-ins; the SL (SME) generally files quarterly Modelo 303 and annual Modelo 390 and remains outside SII unless it opts in. Verifactu (RD 1007/2023) requires all invoicing software to guarantee integrity, authenticity and traceability of invoices, generating structured Facturae/XML output with hash/QR markers; mandatory B2B e-invoicing is being phased in under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), with the SME compliance timeline applying. B2G invoices to Spanish public administrations must be issued electronically in Facturae 3.2 format through the FACe e-invoicing point. OSS and IOSS portals centralize VAT reporting/clearance for intra-EU distance sales, digital services, and low-value import consignments.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Full VAT exemption at a 0% effective rate applies under Article 21.1 LIVA to exports of plush mascot stuffed animals to non-EU destinations, provided the goods physically leave EU customs territory and the exit is evidenced by customs records; transfer of title and risk under the agreed Incoterms is recommended but not a statutory condition. Intra-EU tax-exempt dispatches under Article 25 LIVA require the customer's valid intra-EU VAT ID, the Modelo 349 recapitulative statement, and Intrastat dispatch declarations when thresholds are exceeded. Goods must leave the EU within the customs deadline, generally 90 days from acceptance of the export declaration. The export exemption is not legally conditioned on receipt of payment; however, an Inward Remittance Certificate should be retained and remittance completion is operationally benchmarked at 180 days. Input VAT on raw materials and packaging is recoverable through quarterly Modelo 303 and annual Modelo 390 refund procedures; the monthly REDEME refund regime is optional for qualifying exporters and triggers SII obligations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Documento Unico Administrativo (DUA/SAD) filed electronically via AEAT CEXP/SIL, with customs acceptance and definitive exit validation stamp
Transport and exit evidence - Bill of Lading (maritime), CMR (road), Air Waybill (air) or multimodal warehouse exit records proving physical departure from EU territory
Commercial sales invoice (unit values, Incoterms, quantities, marks) and corresponding packing list
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment evidence showing collection of export proceeds within the 180-day benchmark
Intra-EU evidence where applicable: customer's valid Spanish/EU VAT ID, delivery-field transport documentation, Modelo 349 recapitulative statement, and Intrastat dispatch declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT rigorously audits export substantiation files and requires positive evidence of physical exit or arrival in another Member State, not merely contracts and invoices (CJEU doctrines in Kajot, S s.r.l., Ferens and Mecsek-Gabona). Missing or contradictory proof triggers VAT reassessment at 21% plus late-payment interest and graduated penalties under Articles 191 and 193 LGT: base penalty 50% of the under-declared tax, reducible to 25% on conformity, and increased to 100-150% where fraud or false documentation is used. Undue refund claims are penalized at 50-100% under Article 194 LGT. False export or customs documentation may constitute criminal tax fraud under Article 305 of the Criminal Code where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 (1-5 years imprisonment plus fines) or customs smuggling under Organic Law 12/1995 where values exceed EUR 150,000. The assessment limitation period is four years, subject to suspension and criminal extensions; parties knowingly involved in circular fraud chains may incur joint and several liability under the Kittel doctrine, including retrospective clawback of refunds with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); the European Central Bank is competent for euro monetary policy. Foreign-investment statistical declarations are processed via the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investment (DGCOMIN) under the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a euro-area member with full convertibility and largely unrestricted capital account. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are liberalised under EU free-movement-of-capital rules; there is no requirement to obtain exchange-control approval. Profit remittance and shareholder-loan repayment are not subject to convertibility hurdles. The only frictions are tax-related: general 19% non-resident dividend/interest WHT unless treaty relief or EU Parent-Subsidiary/Interest-Royalty Directive relief is obtained, and post-closing statistical reporting for non-EU investments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Export proceeds in EUR or foreign currency may be retained in any authorised credit institution, fully credited to the exporting SL's treasury account; Spain imposes no mandatory conversion, no surrender ratio and no time bar requiring repatriation of proceeds, although the underlying commercial invoice, customs export declaration and bank reference for balance-of-payments statistical purposes should name the export contract and invoice number.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: FEASIBILITY: LOW as the only banking rail; MEDIUM as an ancillary collection/disbursement sub-rail. LEGAL CONSTRAINTS: a Spanish or EU-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) may open payment accounts, issue e-money, execute SEPA/SWIFT payments and currency exchange, but cannot take deposits or issue commercial letters of credit. An offshore/third-country EMI without an EU licence has no passported right; it can only use a partner bank or request a Spanish bank account as a non-resident MSB, which is normally declined or held to enhanced KYC. Platform_Pay and similar aggregator/correspondent rails may be used for low-value collections, but all treasury balances must sit in a regulated Spanish/EU bank account and not remain on offshore EMI wallet ledger.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal statutory requirement for every director to appear in person for a Spanish SL. Remote onboarding is possible using eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures and live video identification where the final beneficial owner is an EU citizen with a resolvable NIE and no adverse sanctions hit. However, for non-EU directors, corporate opacity, or first capital remittance from outside the EU, Spanish banks commonly require an in-branch interview or a notarised/legalised identity document with apostille. The prudent mandate is to plan at least one physical branch sign-off and notarised corporate resolution before relying on wholly remote banking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from parent in a jurisdiction outside the EEA flagged by transaction-scoring as high source-of-funds risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised/certified statutory deed of the SL, shareholders' resolution approving the capital contribution, ultimate-beneficial-owner declaration, passports/civil registries of all signatories and UBOs, source-of-funds statements covering the transfer path, bank reference letter from the remitting bank, and audited or accountant-verified financial statements of the parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring outbound settlements to PRC/suppliers in Latin America with invoice descriptions inconsistent with import/export declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sales/purchase contracts and purchase orders, original invoices, air/sea waybills, customs entry/export summary for ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930, HS classification and certificate of non-controlled-goods, freight-forwarder and insurance invoices, supplier KYC pack including business registration and sanctions screening, and bank-to-bank correspondence on UETR/MT103 references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors/residents are non-EU tax residents and the SL has little local substance, causing bank de-risking or tax-haven reclassification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish NIE certificates for directors/residents, Censo de empresarios/IAE registration, SL articles and beneficial-ownership registry filings, office lease in Spain, Spanish employee payroll/social-security records, local warehouse or logistics contracts, board minutes appointing local CFO/treasury manager, forward trade and cash-flow forecast matching bank activity to business substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all parental/shareholder funding by bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA credit transfer if remitter is within SEPA and the currency is EUR) directly into the Spanish SL's operational IBAN account. The MT103 remittance information must use an unambiguous purpose phrase such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / SHARE SUBSCRIPTION', 'SHARE PREMIUM' or 'SUBORDINATED SHAREHOLDER LOAN' with the company NIF; it must never be coded as a goods purchase or collection. For EUR receipts no FX conversion occurs. For USD funding, convert against a pre-trade FX forward or on receipt under the bank's spot desk. Verification evidence includes the capital-increase public deed, bank statement, certificate of beneficial owner, NIE, and, where applicable, the DGCOMIN/DataInvex foreign-investment declaration for extra-EU shareholdings above de-minimis thresholds. If the investor is from outside the EU and enters a regulated sector under the EU FDI screening framework, prior filing may be required; for plush-toy OEM this is not ordinarily in scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For raw-material and packaging payments to suppliers in China, Latin America, or Portugal: use SWIFT MT103 TT for immediate settlement (EUR if accepted; otherwise USD), with SWIFT GPI and UETR so all parties can monitor. For pre-production bulk imports and high-value orders, issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700, expressed in EUR/USD, with payment term 30/60 days after bill-of-lading date where possible; confirm by a top-tier bank when the Chinese/LatAm supplier requires confirmation. For Spanish and EU counterparties use SEPA Credit Transfer instant batch. Debit and credit clearing are run through the SL's treasury bank; Platform_Pay may be used only for payouts to micro-collection agents or final B2B channel partners, with the platform wallet funded from the bank, not acting as the sole settlement account. Each settlement must cite invoice/PO, Incoterms, customs declaration, and note whether freight prepaid is reimbursed separately.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forward on EUR/USD and EUR/CNH for forecast export and import flows up to 24 months
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on Latin American currencies (e.g. ARS/COP and selected CNH offshore tenors) only where local deliverability is blocked and the underlying trade exposure is documented
FX swap (swap de divisas) for short-term EUR/USD collateral or working-capital rotation without changing the underlying exposure
Cross-currency basis swap to align capex/shareholder loans denominated in USD with EUR cash-flow, with full EMIR trade reporting
European MiFID II FX options under a client-appropriateness waiver, limited to costless collar structures for trade payables/receivables and prohibited for speculative treasury

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts, including the annual beneficial ownership declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry of the company’s registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Management must prepare accounts within 3 months after the financial year-end; shareholders must approve them within 6 months; filing must occur within 1 month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, filing is generally due by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in administrative fines generally ranging from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to statutory calculation limits. The Commercial Registry may close the company’s registry sheet after 1 year from the filing deadline, preventing registration of most subsequent corporate acts. Continued non-compliance may support administrative dissolution procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the usual deadline is 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior assessment generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay, or 15% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest where applicable. If the Tax Administration assesses the failure, penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder meeting and approval of annual accounts and profit allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; no separate filing authority unless reflected in the Commercial Registry filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the ordinary annual meeting is generally held by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve and file accounts can lead to registry closure, director liability exposure, and fines for late or missing annual-account filing. No separate annual meeting fee applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and updating of beneficial ownership information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and Central Registry of Beneficial Ownership, through the legally prescribed filing and notarial information channels
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Beneficial ownership information must be confirmed in the annual accounts filing and updated when ownership or control changes. Changes should be recorded and reported without undue delay through the applicable registry or notarial process.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or missing beneficial ownership information may cause registry filing defects, prevent completion of related filings, and expose the company and responsible officers to administrative sanctions under Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least 2 of these 3 thresholds for 2 consecutive financial years: total assets above EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover above EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for certain regulated entities, entities issuing securities admitted to trading, and other cases prescribed by law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish accounting regulations. IFRS is generally used for listed groups and may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts; it is not the default framework for an ordinary privately held SL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain accurate ownership and control information, identify the ultimate beneficial owner, confirm the beneficial ownership declaration in the annual accounts filing, and update the information after any change in shareholding or control. Share transfers must be documented in the share-transfer register and reflected in the beneficial ownership records through the applicable legal and notarial channels.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 350-1,300 per year, excluding mail handling, tax representation, and additional compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-7,000 for a small non-complex SL subject to mandatory audit; no statutory audit fee applies where the company is not audit-mandated

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created SLs on the tax base of the first two tax periods with positive tax base (Art. 29.1 LIS); R&D&I tax credits of up to 25% of qualifying expenditure (and 42% on incremental R&D expenditure) under Art. 35 LIS; 12% technological innovation credit; deduction of 25% of export promotion expenses; up to €9,000 per year per new worker with disability; net capitalization reserve of 10% of profit increase (Art. 25 LIS) reducing the tax base up to 10% of positive tax base; successive offsetting of R&D credits. For proprietary plush OEM manufacturing, R&D credits may cover product development of new mascot designs and prototyping. Effective rate can be lowered to approximately 17%-21% with standard credits.
